DSA CP Shared KV Cache

Motivation

DSA prefill context parallelism currently keeps the main MLA KV cache private on
each CP rank. This limits long-context capacity and leaves CP KV movement on
the critical path. This PR adds DSA CP shared KV cache for same-node CP ranks:
the DSA main KV cache is shared in L1 HBM, and DSA L2 HiCache host memory can be
shared by the CP group.

On GLM-5.2-FP8 / H20-3e, the shared path increases allocatable KV capacity by
about 3.47x in L1 HBM and reduces DSA L2 HiCache host memory usage by about
8x in the tested CP=8 configuration. Prefill/TTFT is the first release target,
and shared L2 HiCache host-hit restore reduces TTFT by 37.8% versus base
host-hit in the tested restore workload. Decode is functional and remains an
optimization follow-up.
This makes the current path a good fit for the prefill/P side of PD
disaggregation, while D-side decode optimization continues.

Summary of the current measured result:

  • L1 HBM KV capacity: 3.47x higher allocatable KV tokens.
  • L2 HiCache host memory: about 8x lower DSA KV/indexer host memory across
    the CP group by using one owner allocation plus follower attachments.
  • L1 prefill/TTFT: roughly on par with base, within about 2% in the main
    release target scenario.
  • L1 decode: functional, with a current +7.6% TPOT gap to optimize in the
    4k input / 1k output / b10 benchmark.
  • L2 HiCache host-hit restore: 37.8% lower TTFT than base host-hit in the
    tested restore workload.

Modifications

  • Add --enable-dsa-cp-shared-kv-cache for same-node DSA CP shared KV.
  • Introduce a reusable SharedKV layout helper for rank-major slot translation
    and L2 transfer-index selection; DSA CP is the first adapter.
  • Share the DSA main KV cache in L1 HBM with a rank-major VMM layout, so CP
    ranks can read peer KV directly instead of materializing a full private copy.
  • Share DSA L2 HiCache host memory within the CP group, using the same
    owner/follower synchronization shape as SharedMLA (feat(hicache): shared L2 KV cache pool for MLA models (SharedMLA) #28027).
  • Replace the former KV all-gather happens-before edge with a mandatory CP write
    fence before peer KV reads.
  • Keep DSA indexer HBM private in this phase, and add tests/docs for the L1/L2
    shared main-KV path.

Design Notes

  • L1 uses a rank-major shared KV layout. Each CP rank writes its owner pages;
    attention reads through the translated global page table.
  • L2 uses shared host memory for the DSA main KV. Rank 0 owns storage backup,
    and restore writes each rank's owner shard back into local HBM.
  • The shared-KV layout helper is generic, while this PR only enables the DSA
    adapter.

Capacity

GLM-5.2-FP8 on H20-3e, tp=8, attn_cp=8, kv-cache-dtype=fp8_e4m3,
mem-fraction-static=0.86.

path allocatable KV tokens relative capacity
base 339,712 1.00x
shared 1,179,200 3.47x

Example capacity logs:

KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.float8_e4m3fn, #tokens: 339712
KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.float8_e4m3fn, #tokens: 1179200
DSA CP shared L2 host memory: create/attach ... kind=dsa_l2

The gain is below cp_size because DSA indexer HBM remains private per rank in
this phase.

Correctness And Accuracy

  • Code checks passed: py_compile, git diff --check, and the DSA shared KV
    unit tests.
  • Serving checks passed for fixed greedy prompts and long-context P-side
    output=1 cases; cache hits were 0.
  • Community accuracy sanity with python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval:
eval examples base score shared score delta
GSM8K 200 0.630 0.650 +2.0 pp
MMLU 64 0.750 0.796875 +4.6875 pp

These small-sample evals do not show an accuracy regression; positive deltas are
treated as sampling variance.

Performance

Official sglang.benchmark.serving, dataset random-ids, flush-cache,
cache hit 0.0%, same pod/model/server configuration.

Startup command:

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30080 \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --attn-cp-size 8 \
  --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-total-tokens 131072 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.86 \
  --enable-cache-report \
  --skip-server-warmup \
  --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse \
  --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32

Shared adds:

--enable-dsa-cp-shared-kv-cache

Benchmark command shape:

python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30080 \
  --dataset-name random-ids \
  --model /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --tokenizer /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --num-prompts ${BATCH} \
  --random-input-len ${INPUT_LEN} \
  --random-output-len ${OUTPUT_LEN} \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency ${BATCH} \
  --output-file ${OUTPUT_FILE} \
  --output-details \
  --disable-tqdm \
  --cache-report \
  --flush-cache \
  --warmup-requests 0 \
  --seed 740

Prefill / TTFT benchmark:

workload path actual concurrency TTFT mean delta vs base
32k input / 1 output / b1 base 1.00 3211.11 ms baseline
32k input / 1 output / b1 shared 1.00 3240.08 ms +0.9%

4k input / 1k output / b10 base 9.99 30.87 ms 30.45 ms 293.00 tok/s baseline

L2 HiCache host-hit benchmark:

The L2 restore run uses the same serving configuration plus:

--max-total-tokens 131072 \
--enable-hierarchical-cache \
--hicache-ratio 10 \
--hicache-write-policy write_through \
--hicache-io-backend kernel \
--hicache-mem-layout page_first
workload path L2 state host cached tokens TTFT mean delta
100k input / 1 output / b1 shared cold 0 11007.29 ms reference
100k input / 1 output / b1 base host hit 104,832 1071.94 ms baseline
100k input / 1 output / b1 shared host hit 104,832 666.30 ms -37.8% vs base host hit

The cached-token count is page-rounded, so it can be slightly larger than the
prompt token count.

Interpretation:

  • Prefill/TTFT is treated as roughly on par with base in the current phase-1
    path; small positive/negative deltas are within benchmark noise.
  • L2 host-hit restore is substantially faster than cold prefill; for the
    host-hit path itself, shared L2 reduces TTFT by 37.8% versus base in the
    tested 100k workload.
  • Decode TPOT is slower in this benchmark and remains the main optimization
    item.
  • The shared path is useful for long-context capacity and P-side workloads in PD
    disaggregation. D-side decode remains supported and will continue to be
    optimized.

Follow-Ups

  • Optimize FlashMLA KV decode over shared VMM mappings to reduce the TPOT gap.
  • Evaluate HBM indexer sharing separately after L1/L2 main KV sharing lands.
  • Extend the same correctness/performance matrix to Eagle/MTP after the base DSA
    shared KV path is stable.
  • Consider extending the generic shared-KV layout adapter to other KV layouts
    once another backend needs the same L1/L2 sharing model.

Co-authored with @foraxe

Code Review

This pull request introduces support for DSA CP (Context Parallel) shared KV cache in L1 HBM and HiCache L2, adding a CUDA VMM-based peer-mapped shared memory utility and updating the attention backend, cache controllers, and memory pools. The review feedback highlights several critical issues: potential resource leaks of virtual address space and mapped segments during exceptions in VMM mapping, a file descriptor leak in the POSIX FD exchange upon timeout or failure, a potential Triton compilation error due to mismatched pointer types when output_dtype is specified, and a missing synchronization barrier in move_kv_cache when copying KV cache across ranks.

Choose a reason for hiding this comment

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more.

If an exception occurs during the mapping loop, any successfully mapped segments are not unmapped, and the reserved virtual address range base_va is leaked. We should unmap the mapped segments using cuMemUnmap and free the reserved virtual address range using cuMemAddressFree before re-raising the exception.

Suggested change
except Exception:
for handle in imported_handles:
drv.cuMemRelease(handle)
raise
except Exception:
for i in range(len(mapped_handles)):
try:
drv.cuMemUnmap(int(base_va) + i * aligned_bytes, aligned_bytes)
except Exception:
pass
try:
drv.cuMemAddressFree(base_va, total_bytes)
except Exception:
pass
for handle in imported_handles:
try:
drv.cuMemRelease(handle)
except Exception:
pass
raise

There was a problem hiding this comment.

Choose a reason for hiding this comment

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more.

If output_dtype is specified and differs from slot_indices.dtype (e.g., int32 vs int64), src and dst passed to dsa_cp_shared_slot_indices_kernel will have different pointer types. Inside the Triton kernel, storing int64 values into an int32* pointer will cause a compilation error or undefined behavior. We should cast slot_indices to output_dtype first to ensure matching types.

Suggested change
if not slot_indices.is_cuda:
return None
out = torch.empty_like(slot_indices, dtype=output_dtype or slot_indices.dtype)
if not slot_indices.is_cuda:
return None
if output_dtype is not None and slot_indices.dtype != output_dtype:
slot_indices = slot_indices.to(output_dtype)
out = torch.empty_like(slot_indices)

There was a problem hiding this comment.

Choose a reason for hiding this comment

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more.

In a context parallel multi-GPU setup, copying KV cache across ranks via peer-mapped shared memory requires synchronization. Without an explicit barrier, a rank might read stale data from another rank's segment before the write is completed, or subsequent operations might read from the local segment before the write finishes. Also, any barrier must be executed by all ranks collectively to avoid hanging, so we should not return early before the barrier.

Suggested change
if self.enable_cp_shared_kvcache:
mask = self._owned_cp_shared_write_mask(tgt_loc_flat)
if not torch.any(mask):
return
local_tgt = self._translate_cp_shared_write_loc(tgt_loc_flat[mask])
shared_src = self.translate_loc_to_cp_shared_device(src_loc_flat[mask])
for local_kv_cache, global_kv_cache in zip(
self.cp_shared_kv_buffer, self.kv_buffer
):
local_kv_cache[local_tgt] = global_kv_cache[shared_src]
return
